title: Reduced stationary uniqueness and explicit research boundaries

items.title: Positive matrix harmonic-map boundary problem
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d,n\in\mathbb N$ with $d,n\ge1$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is locally the graph of a smooth function. Here $C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ means restriction of a smooth function on an open neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$. Use the matrix spaces $M_n(\mathbb C)$ and ordinary matrix multiplication. For $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ write $A^\dagger:=\overline A^{\mathsf T}$, and write $\operatorname{tr}A:=\sum_{j<n}A_{jj}$. A matrix $\Phi$ is **positive definite Hermitian** when $\Phi^\dagger=\Phi$ and $v^\dagger\Phi v$ is a positive real number for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb C^n$. Define

$$\mathcal P_n:=\{\Phi\in M_n(\mathbb C):\Phi\text{ is positive definite Hermitian and }\det\Phi=1\}.$$

The determinant is the determinant over $\mathbb C$. Every $\Phi\in\mathcal P_n$ is invertible because $\det\Phi=1$ is a unit; its inverse is smooth when $\Phi$ is a smooth matrix field because the adjugate formula reduces to polynomial entries when $\det\Phi=1$.

For a smooth map $\Phi:\overline\Omega\to\mathcal P_n$, define the matrix-valued one-form $d\Phi=\sum_{a=1}^d(\partial_a\Phi)\,dx^a$ by differentiating entries, and put $J:=\Phi^{-1}d\Phi=\sum_{a=1}^d J_a\,dx^a$. Its **matrix harmonic-map equation** in this item means exactly

$$\operatorname{div}J:=\sum_{a=1}^d\partial_aJ_a=0\quad\text{on }\Omega.$$

The positive matrix boundary problem is to compare two such maps $\Phi_0,\Phi_1$ satisfying this equation and prescribed values on all of $\partial\Omega$. The Euclidean coordinates, matrix size, determinant normalization, and divergence convention are part of the definition. No spacetime metric, symmetry reduction, physical postulate, or spacetime uniqueness theorem is included.

items.title: Positive-matrix comparison identity
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d,n\ge1$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be the nonempty bounded connected smooth domain of [[def-emg-fx-matrix-harmonic-problem]]. Let $\Phi_0,\Phi_1\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathcal P_n)$ satisfy $\operatorname{div}J_i=0$, where $J_i:=\Phi_i^{-1}d\Phi_i=\sum_{a=1}^dJ_{i,a}\,dx^a$ and $\operatorname{div}J_i:=\sum_a\partial_aJ_{i,a}$. Define

$$\Psi:=\Phi_1\Phi_0^{-1}-I_n,\qquad \Delta J_a:=J_{1,a}-J_{0,a}.$$

Then, pointwise on $\Omega$,

$$\Delta\operatorname{tr}\Psi=\sum_{a=1}^d\operatorname{tr}\!\left((\Delta J_a)^\dagger\Phi_1\Delta J_a\Phi_0^{-1}\right)\ge0,$$

where $\Delta=\sum_a\partial_a^2$ is the Euclidean Laplacian. If $\Phi_1=\Phi_0$ on the entire boundary $\partial\Omega$, then $\Phi_1=\Phi_0$ on $\overline\Omega$. This is an abstract bounded-domain uniqueness result for the stated positive matrix equation.

items.title: Stationary-axisymmetric geometry and circularity domain
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with smooth future timelike time-orientation field $N$, and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty connected open set. A **stationary field on $U$** is a specified smooth Killing field $k$ that is timelike on a specified nonempty open subset of $U$; no normalization or global timelikeness is inferred.

Here $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with complex multiplication and the smooth circle-group structure fixed in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. An **axial $U(1)$ action on $U$** is a specified smooth map $\rho:U(1)\times U\to U$ satisfying $\rho(1,p)=p$ and $\rho(z_1z_2,p)=\rho(z_1,\rho(z_2,p))$, with $\rho(z,\cdot)^*g=g$ for every $z$; effective means that only $z=1$ acts identically on all of $U$. Its generator is the smooth vector field $m$ defined by $m_p=\frac{d}{d\theta}|_{\theta=0}\rho(e^{i\theta},p)$; the parameter has period $2\pi$. Its **axis** is the fixed-point set $\mathcal A:=\{p\in U:\rho(z,p)=p\text{ for every }z\in U(1)\}$. For this page, an **axisymmetric region** is a region supplied with such an effective action and satisfying $g(m,m)>0$ on $U\setminus\mathcal A$. A stationary field and axial generator **commute** when their Lie bracket vanishes; in coordinates this means $\sum_a(k^a\partial_a m^b-m^a\partial_a k^b)=0$ for every component $b$.

Define

$$U_*:=\{p\in U\setminus\mathcal A:k_p,m_p\text{ are linearly independent and }g_p|_{\operatorname{span}\{k_p,m_p\}}\text{ is nondegenerate}\}.$$

Because $M$ is Hausdorff, each fixed set $\{p:\rho(z,p)=p\}$ is closed in $U$: it is the preimage of the closed diagonal in $U\times U$ under $p\mapsto(\rho(z,p),p)$. Their intersection $\mathcal A$ is closed, so $U\setminus\mathcal A$ is open. In a chart, linear independence is witnessed by a nonzero $2\times2$ minor of the $4\times2$ coordinate matrix with columns $k$ and $m$, and nondegeneracy is $\det G\ne0$ for the continuous Gram matrix $G_{ij}:=g(K_i,K_j)$, where $K_1:=k$ and $K_2:=m$. These are open conditions, so $U_*$ is open. On $U_*$ the matrix $G$ is invertible. Its inverse entries are smooth by the cofactor-over-determinant formula. The smooth map

$$\Pi_p(v):=\sum_{i,j=1}^2K_i(p)(G(p)^{-1})_{ij}g_p(K_j(p),v)$$

is a projection onto $\operatorname{span}\{k,m\}$, since it fixes each $K_i$ and $v-\Pi_p(v)$ is orthogonal to both generators. Therefore

$$\mathcal D_p:=\ker\Pi_p=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,k_p)=g_p(v,m_p)=0\}$$

is a smooth rank-two distribution on $U_*$: the projection has rank two in each tangent space, and its kernel has dimension $4-2=2$. The kernel varies smoothly because, locally, a nonzero two-by-two minor lets one solve its two linear equations smoothly for two components in terms of the other two.

An **immersed surface through $p$** here means the image of a smooth immersion $\sigma:S\to U_*$ from a two-dimensional smooth manifold $S$, with $p\in\sigma(S)$; immersion means that $d\sigma_q:T_qS\to T_{\sigma(q)}U_*$ is injective for every $q\in S$. Its tangent plane at $\sigma(q)$ is $d\sigma_q(T_qS)$. **Circularity on $U_*$** means that through every point of $U_*$ there is such a local immersed surface with $d\sigma_q(T_qS)=\mathcal D_{\sigma(q)}$ at every point of its domain.

These are supplied geometric data and definitions. They assert no existence of a second Killing field, no symmetry inheritance from matter equations, no integrability of $\mathcal D$, no global smooth quotient or orbit-space boundary structure, and no Einstein–Maxwell solution. Any use of the causal or horizon terms follows [[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. A future spacetime theorem must state any extra asymptotic, horizon, axis-regularity, analyticity, connectedness and nondegeneracy hypotheses it uses.

items.title: What remains before a stationary electrovacuum uniqueness theorem
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
The positive-matrix theorem on this page is an abstract Euclidean boundary result. Its matrices and Dirichlet boundary do not encode a spacetime, a horizon, or a global Einstein–Maxwell solution. The geometry terms used for any possible application have the exact local conventions of the stationary-axisymmetric setup defined earlier on this page. In particular, the stationary field is specified and is timelike only on its declared open subset; the axial symmetry is a specified periodic isometric $U(1)$ action; and circularity is the integrability of the rank-two distribution orthogonal to the commuting generators where their span is nondegenerate.

The current draft spherical local-rigidity result assumes its exact Einstein–Maxwell–$\Lambda$ quotient equations and requires both $dr\ne0$ and $q^{-1}(dr,dr)\ne0$ throughout the chosen patch. Its conclusion is a local RN–(A)dS form; constant-radius patches, null-gradient patches, global extensions and stationary-axisymmetric uniqueness are outside its Statement. It is a separate spherical result, not the missing global orbit-space theorem.

The published sphere-winding lemma's product-circle calculation has zero curvature and nontrivial principal holonomy for a nonintegral parameter, while the published local-potential definition allows chartwise potentials and records their transition data. Thus a future reduction must state each one-form whose primitive is used, prove the required local or global exactness, or retain the relevant bundle sectors. This includes scalar functions conventionally used in Ernst and twist reductions; their specific differential definitions and existence conditions must be stated before use. Stationarity alone does not supply global scalar potentials.

The source treatments show why the matrix identity cannot be transferred by name alone. The general comparison identity can be written before imposing a second symmetry, but the black-hole uniqueness application also needs the axial reduction and positivity conditions. Reduction using a stationary Killing field can change the target signature where that field becomes null or spacelike; the positive Hermitian representation therefore needs proof on the actual domain. A spacetime argument must separately establish symmetry inheritance (for example, invariance of the Maxwell two-form under both specified generators), commutation, circularity, the global smooth quotient and its boundary structure, regularity on the axis and any selected null horizon, and the falloff conditions on any declared asymptotic end. It must then control the boundary terms in the comparison argument under those exact hypotheses. The 1996 textbook supplies a proof for a restricted Kerr–Newman class with its own axis, horizon and infinity analysis; that result is not imported here. The 2012 review also distinguishes the local matrix identity from the global boundary step.

This page asserts no stationary electrovacuum uniqueness theorem, no dynamical stability result, and no cosmic-censorship conclusion. It makes no blanket current-status claim about broader uniqueness or stability questions.

title: Reduced stationary uniqueness and explicit research boundaries — Examples

items.title: A scalar diagonal sector of the positive matrix equation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be the nonempty bounded connected smooth Euclidean domain of the positive matrix boundary problem, with $d\ge1$. For a smooth real-valued function $u$ on $\overline\Omega$, define the Euclidean Laplacian by $\Delta u:=\sum_{a=1}^d\partial_a^2u$ and call $u$ **harmonic** on $\Omega$ when $\Delta u=0$ there. In matrix size $n=2$, define

$$\Phi_u(x):=\begin{pmatrix}e^{u(x)}&0\\0&e^{-u(x)}\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then $\Phi_u$ is a smooth map into the positive Hermitian determinant-one matrices, and it satisfies $\operatorname{div}(\Phi_u^{-1}d\Phi_u)=0$ exactly when $u$ is harmonic. If two such maps have identical values at every boundary point, then they agree on $\overline\Omega$.
